summary: ⇒: h(s, t) = h(γ⁻¹s, γ⁻¹t) and for vectors orthogonal to X only the middle parts count. ⇐: an annihilator argument produces the vector t.

steps.claim: ⇒ (the link is isotropic): for p = (t_mid, (γ⁻¹t)_mid) and q = (s_mid, (γ⁻¹s)_mid) with s, t ⊥ X + γX, h(s, t) = h(γ⁻¹s, γ⁻¹t) (γ is unitary), and for vectors with zero e*-parts h reduces to T on the middle parts; so q̄ᵀ diag(T, −T) p = T(s_mid, t_mid) − T((γ⁻¹s)_mid, (γ⁻¹t)_mid) = 0.

steps.claim: ⇐ (the link is maximal isotropic): suppose p is orthogonal to the whole link. By exists_mulVec_eq_of_annihilator (for the matrices 1 and γ, free e-coordinates, targets (0, p₁, 0) and (0, p₂, 0)) it suffices to check l(0, p₁, 0) = l(γ(0, p₂, 0)) for every linear form l vanishing on the e-columns of 1 and of γ. Writing l = h(t, ·) (exists_star_vecMul_eq) and moving γ across (J γ⁻¹ = γᴴ J), these conditions say t ⊥ X and γ⁻¹t ⊥ X, so (t_mid, (γ⁻¹t)_mid) lies in the link and the orthogonality of p to it is the required equality. The vectors obtained exhibit p ∈ link(γ).
